- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is rising (≥0.36) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to prevent over-optimism.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.18–0.36), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use 10-day SMA to anchor forecast if price deviates >2% from recent 5-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overpredict early in the window; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days if sentiment is weak or volatile.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.18–0.27), model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to compensate for suppressed momentum.
